title: 2026-03-28 Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Stratus Financial
next_steps: Send updated pricing for 2x reserved capacity + EU region by 2026-04-02
Share SOC2 + ISO docs and VPC deployment guide by 2026-03-30
Schedule benchmark with Marco and Samira for week of 2026-04-06
Draft contract amendment for 12-month extension and new SKUs by 2026-04-09
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer is evaluating a capacity bump to dedicated GPUs, adding EU region and possibly APAC over next 6 months. Procurement requested updated pricing for a 12-month extension. Engineering concerned about latency and regional failover; asked for benchmark and SOC2 docs. Agreed next steps and timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - Jordan from Redwood here. Looks like we have about 45 minutes, trying to cover renewal details and the capacity ask.
[00:07] Priya Singh: Hey Jordan, hi Samira. Yes, we got the calendar, thanks. Whole team here - Marco, Dana, Evan. Quick background: our contract up in July, and usage has grown about 3x Q/Q, happy with quality but hitting throughput limits.
[00:20] Samira Patel: Great, appreciate that context. Quick qual: is the 3x spike primarily synchronous inference for customer chat, or embeddings/batch as well?
[00:27] Priya Singh: Mostly chat - low-latency generation for agent assist. We also do batch embeddings overnight but that’s less urgent.
[00:33] Marco Ruiz: From infra side, the big ask is predictable throughput. We tried the hosted bursts but saw latency variance during peak; we want dedicated pools with autoscale and a region in eu-west to reduce RTT for EU users.
[00:45] Jordan Reyes: Totally makes sense. For dedicated we can provision reserved GPU capacity. Did you have a target p50/p95 latency you need to hit?
[00:52] Evan Park: p50 under 120ms, p95 under 300ms for 512-token responses. We can tolerate a few spikes but that’s the baseline.
[00:58] Samira Patel: Ok cool. For 512 tokens those SLAs are achievable on our optimized runtime with the right instance sizing and batch config. I’ll note we typically recommend a mix of 2x rtx A40-like units for your load pattern initially and then autoscale.
[01:10] Dana Lee: On procurement - we need updated pricing for a 12-month extension that includes the dedicated pool and EU region. Also can you include add-on cost for APAC region?
[01:18] Jordan Reyes: Yes we can. We’ll put together two pricing bundles: (A) 2x reserved capacity + EU region; (B) 2x reserved + EU + APAC reserved (or burst). We’ll price both for 12-month term and include unit economics for on-demand vs reserved.
[01:30] Priya Singh: One question about data residency and logs - our compliance team requires that EU traffic and logs remain within the EU region. Can Redwood support region-scoped audit logs and KMS per region?
[01:41] Samira Patel: Yes - our private and dedicated offerings support region-specific key management. For hosted we have regional log segregation for EU and can integrate with customer-managed KMS in the EU for the dedicated/private control plane. There might be a small ops lead time to onboard the customer's KMS.
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: How about certs and SOC2 evidence? We have an internal checklist.
[02:00] Jordan Reyes: We’ll share SOC2, ISO artifacts, and our VPC deployment runbook. Expect the docs by early next week.
[02:06] Dana Lee: Great. For timelines: if we sign an amendment by mid-April can you stand up EU region in May?
[02:12] Samira Patel: That’s reasonable. I’ll work with infra - for dedicated reserved we need provisioning lead time plus any KMS onboarding, so May is doable if paperwork and payment clear by mid-April.
[02:22] Priya Singh: We also want to run a throughput benchmark simulating our traffic - can Redwood run a bench with our traces and show expected latency/throughput?
[02:30] Samira Patel: Yes - we usually do a benchmark run. Marco, we’ll need a sample trace and target qps. We can provision a test pool identical to the proposed dedicated config and run both p50/p95 and end-to-end RTT.
[02:40] Marco Ruiz: I’ll send over traces and a qps target by Friday. Expect some tokenization differences but should be close.
[02:46] Jordan Reyes: Awesome. On pricing: just to set expectations, moving to reserved capacity gives about 30-40% unit cost reduction vs on-demand and also priority for capacity. For EU/APAC add-ons there’s a regional surcharge for infra and data residency ops. We’ll detail in the quote.
[03:03] Evan Park: Any concerns about fallback if EU region has transient issues? We need multi-region failover policy.
[03:09] Samira Patel: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in another region. We’ll work with you to set routing policy: prefer EU, failover to NA with redaction or additional consent as needed. That part does require config in the control plane.
[03:23] Priya Singh: Ok - another thing: are there model variants we should consider for cost savings? We sometimes sacrifice a bit of throughput for cheaper model which performs fine for lower-priority flows.
[03:33] Samira Patel: Yes - our Optimize toolkit recommends quantized or smaller variants for background jobs. For chat, we can A/B test a cheaper variant for non-critical sessions. We can include recommendations in the quote.
[03:43] Dana Lee: Procurement also wants contract language around uptime SLA and credits. What are your standard SLA terms for Dedicated?
[03:49] Jordan Reyes: Standard Dedicated SLA is 99.9% with credits for downtime tiers; we can share the SLA appendix. For enterprise deals we sometimes negotiate stricter SLAs - we can surface that to legal if needed.
[04:01] Evan Park: One last technical: KV cache persistence - if we failover region, does cache warm-up cause latency cliffs?
[04:09] Samira Patel: There’s some KV warming cost; our routing can use prefix caching and pre-warm critical prefixes. We’ll show expected cold-start behavior in the benchmark report.
[04:18] Jordan Reyes: To recap next steps: Jordan/Jordan? (laughs) I will compile pricing options and send by Friday; Samira will run benchmark once Marco shares traces; we’ll share SOC2/ISO and VPC runbook; Dana to review procurement terms and confirm target sign date mid-April.
[04:34] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: Thanks.
[04:37] Dana Lee: Thanks all.
[04:38] Jordan Reyes: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts and speaker overlaps. There were a few places where acronyms were slightly garbled (KMS referenced as "KMS" and once as "KM S").
